question.text: Chambal Managed Futures Fund is being structured as a Category III AIF. Which statement correctly reflects the fund-structure options available under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Cat III AIFs must be close-ended, like Cat I and II
Cat III AIFs may be either open-ended or close-ended, as structured at registration
Cat III AIFs must be open-ended and close-ended funds are prohibited
Cat III AIFs can convert from open to close-ended annually with SEBI approval

explanation.text: The Logic: Schemes of all Category III AIFs are either open-ended OR close-ended, as structured by the Sponsor/Manager at the time of registration. This flexibility is UNIQUE to Cat III; Cat I and Cat II must be close-ended. The Trap: Option A applies Cat I/II rule. Option C is opposite extreme. Option D invents a conversion feature. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-D tests 'Cat I/II must be close-ended'. XIX-E tests the Cat III flexibility — a defining feature. Manager's Pro-Tip: Open-ended structure enables daily NAV, quarterly/monthly redemptions, HWM crystallisation — the standard hedge-fund chassis. Close-ended is typical for event-driven/illiquid-bias Cat III strategies where lock-up serves risk management.
